reviews.title: Amazing app!
reviews.text: The new WW app has so many features that aid in a successful weight loss/ health journey. Tracking is essential, and once you learn where everything is, it’s simple to track meals. ( I do have one suggestion, however, that when presented with a search item, say kale, for example, that the list that comes up should always start with the uncooked version, then the cooked version(from simple to more complex) as opposed to finding a simple iteration among various commercial offerings, making it harder to find😉) The help feature is great once you get past the bots and get to a real person☺️ Fantastic people who will work with you to solve any problem, technical or plan related. The recipes are so helpful! I like that you can scroll through and find recipes you might use later, and then save them to your list of My Foods, or save them to your plan. I use the recipe creator regularly to decide if a meal I want to eat fits into my day or days ahead. Then if I decide not to use right away, I can save it for future reference, so my time was not wasted. I recently tried one of the Walk and Talk podcasts when I took my daily walk. I listened to Oprah… found it to be helpful in keeping that important mindset, and interesting as well. I am a lifetime WW member, so I have seen a lot of change over the last 30 years. It gets better and better! The WW team has really come up with an all-incompassing app to aid us in the difficult process of permanent weight loss and health. I know it has played a major role in my overall success with the program. Addendum 8-23-25 to this post that was not sent??? I love the recent addition of breakdown of nutrients of food eaten. This is so valuable!!!! Thank you.

reviews.title: Very Helpful Staying On Track
reviews.text:
Overall, really nice and very helpful. Key pros: 
 1. Awesome volume of items available by scanning the UPC or by searching by name. 
 2. Easily look at foods and their impact before tracking them to a meal. 
 3. Ability to easily move tracked foods from one meal to another. 
 4. Can create your own foods and recipes. 
 5. Tracks nutrition info in addition to WW points so fine-tuning your diet is easy. 
 6. Slightly different point values when set to Diabetes mode. Helpful for diabetics to avoid higher carb foods that are “free” to others. 
 7. “Saved” foods list makes it easier to track specific brands or differences like cooked vs uncooked. 

A few areas that could be improved (Cons):
 1. When searching for foods by name, order the list so that “saved” foods come up first. They were saved for a reason. 
 2. Allow sharing custom foods the way that custom recipes can already be shared. 

That’s really it for the cons, but #1 is annoying enough that it dropped the overall rating by a point all by itself.

reviews.title: Lifetime Member
reviews.text:
This is my 42nd year of being a Lifetime member of WW (formerly Weight Watchers) The strategies and techniques and knowledge (and now technology) learned -when put into daily practice-have resulted in 4 decades of healthy habits and continue to allow me to maintain a healthy weight for my age and height. Thank you WW. Learning new point values daily and evolving with the new program strategies keeps me learning new ways to enjoy food as my friend. Weight maintenance is my goal. I have been tracking daily for over 1550 consecutive days. Tracking honestly and daily is an integral key to success, as knowing what I am eating and how much matters in weight loss, habit changes, wise choices, and seeing food as my friend as well as a blessing. I only need a dime size taste of something to try it and then I feel satisfied. Being able to say that “I can eat anything” is a gift and positive and eliminates the “deprivation mindset.” 
Information is power. Everyday I learn something new, try new foods and meals, and mindfully eat healthy foods for my body. Grateful. Praying and making wise choices-with food and with everything, including tracking, weighing, measuring.  Activities I strive for include personal exercising, gym strength training, mindful moving, daily walking after meals, vacation exercise, walking on the beach, stationary bike at home, dancing, walking for steps, working, and living fully and joyfully with these practiced and recorded daily habits. I am thankful for a healthy body and mind and medicine free, thank God. Prayer helps, too. Thank you WW! Celebrating life! Carpé diem. Seizing my days with healthy living.

I was 243 back in March and I’m down to 180 pounds now and I’ve been at 180 pounds for the last month, I don’t feel that I need to lose more. I’m happy being comfortable in smaller clothing.
The greatest thing with the app is going to a restaurant and putting their menu in the search to which every item on that menu shows you a point value. This got me selecting the Dallas fillet instead of the Fort Worth ribeye at Texas roadhouse and also made me aware that their baked potatoes have points whereas at home they do not and this is attributed to them coating them with Oil. I’ve learned about avoiding Oil is the key and how that’s a sneaky thing in our foods that causes us to gain weight. Thank you for taking time to read this and thank you again for making Weight Watchers better than it has ever been!

Then when I log the meals and snacks , and run out of points one or two days I reevaluate and make plans to buckle up and use less points , increase my steps and exercise next days to have balance .WW teaches us discipline and self control .I believe the key is perseverance and logging daily .I don’t feel deprived because nothing is forbidden . Just small portions in food rich in points , foods like cakes , chocolate and ice cream that I ❤️ 🏆

reviews.title: Big Part of My Life Now
reviews.text:
I have lost 15 pounds on the weight watchers app. It is a big part of my life now, and actually feel like it’s a fun game to keep track of my food, weight, exercise, and water. I’ll probably keep doing the app even after I reach my goal! Thank you Weight Watchers! 

UPDATE #1: 22 lbs!
UPDATE #2: 29 lbs!
UPDATE #3: 41 lbs!

I wish there was a way to inform WW of app improvement suggestions. The tabs that I never use, like Discover GLP1, are always present at the bottom of the screen and the tabs I use everyday are less accessible, like weight entry.
